Page 1/11 
Machine Learning (BMI/GEO/WNA) 
Code Assignment U1A1  
Linear Regression 
This is NOT a group Assignment. 
 
10 marks 
Please complete seeing the videos for Week 1-2 before attempting this 
assignment.  
 
Use real estate valuation regression dataset : 
https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/477/real+estate+valuation+data+set  from 
the UCI repository, and use google colab to code. 
 
First, download the csv file, and open it in your computer and analyze the data. 
Try to understand what the data is about. Read through the data description 
given 
in 
the 
UCI 
website 
as 
well. 
 
Section A 
Answer the following questions [1 mark if you answer all the below questions]: 
1. How many samples are there? 
Ans) 414 
2. How 
many 
input 
variables 
are 
there? 
Ans) 6 
3. Which 
column 
is 
the 
output 
variable 
(target 
outcome)? 
 
Ans) House price of unit area 
4. What does each of the input columns mean? 
 Ans)  
X1 transaction date: e.g. 2012.917 indicates 2012 September, 2012 Year 
and .917 indicates the month (September) of the year 
            X2 house age: Age of the house at the time of transaction e.g. 19.5      
indicates 19 years and 5 months

Page 2/11 
X3 distance to the nearest MRT station: Distance from the property to nearest 
MRT (Mass Rapid Transit) station. E.g. 84.87882 meter is the distance 
X4 number of convenience stores: Count of convenient stores closest to the 
property 
 
X5 latitude: Location of the property (geographic coordinate that indicates 
North-South direction of the property) 
 
X6 longitude: Location of the property (geographic coordinate that indicates 
East-West direction of the property) 
 
Section B 
For each of the questions below, you need to put in the screenshot of the code 
and its output. You could use the sample google colab file that is provided with 
this assignment. 
 
1. Understanding the dataset [4 marks] 
There are many input variables in this dataset. Use only X1 to X4 as input 
variables, and y as the output variable. 
Using the scatter plots between each of the input features (X1-X4) and the 
output (Y), which input variable, do you think, is better in predicting the output 
/ target variable ? 
Ans) Distance to the nearest MRT station is better in predicting the output 
variable because from this plot we could identify that as the distance to the MRT 
station increases house price of unit area decreases.

Page 3/11

3. What is the train test split ratio that you have chosen? [1 Mark] 
Ans) Train test split ratio = 70:30

Page 4/11 
 
Training set = (2/3) * 414 = 276 samples 
Test set = (1/3) * 414 = 138 samples
